title: Kubaneh (Yemeni Buttery Pull-Apart Bread)
summary: Thin buttered sheets of dough rolled into coils, packed into a lidded pot and baked long and slow until deeply browned.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
butter, very soft, plus extra for the pot

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt with the water and knead 10 min until smooth and very stretchy.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave about 1 h until doubled. Butter the pot well.

steps.title: Stretch
steps.text: Divide into 8 balls. Smear the worktop with butter, then press and stretch each ball into a very thin sheet, spread with soft butter, fold the sides in and roll up into a rope.

steps.title: Coil
steps.text: Curl each rope into a snail and set them snugly in the pot; cover and leave 45 min until puffy. Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake with the lid on 40 min, then lower to 120 °C (100 °C fan) and bake 2-3 h more until deep mahogany brown underneath.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Turn out and serve warm; pull the coils apart by hand.

tips: Use plenty of butter on the worktop and your hands.
Keep the lid on so the bread stays soft inside.
Serve with grated tomato and hot green chilli sauce.
storage: Best warm on the day; rewarm wrapped in foil. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
